title: Boot-time dual-SE attestation with factory-pinned UIDs plus a C10 MCU attestation command (AuthenticateDevice analogue), bound to the FSBL measurement
threat: Chip swap (OPTIGA or SE050) in transit or after sale; a cloned board with genuine-looking firmware; a stolen device re-shelled around a fresh MCU — none detected today because no code reads an SE attestation object, pins SE UIDs, or lets the companion challenge the unit remotely.
proposal: (1) At boot, after SCP03/Shielded sessions are up: read OPTIGA UID (0xE0C2) and the SE050 chipId, compare against the per-device binding record (already specified 3× in threat-model §9.4 rows; store the SHA-256 anchor in the OTP birth record from BOOT-04); mismatch after first-boot ALL_DONE → admin-wipe path. Verify a fresh-nonce signature from each SE's factory cert (OPTIGA 0xE0E3 type-0x12 device cert already present; SE050 C-class 0xF0000013) against the Infineon/NXP roots pinned in the image — the SE is the signer, so invariant #5 (no classical signer in the WALLET) holds; document that these are vendor-mandated verifications like dbgen's EAS fence. (2) Add `CMD_ATTEST_DEVICE`: the secure world signs `'pq1-attest:' || compactsize(challenge) || challenge || secure_digest` with a SPHINCS+C10 key derived per use from SAES-CMAC(DHUK, 'attest') (never stored), whose public key the factory certifies into the per-unit record; companion verifies chain + both SE proofs; stream the 4008-B signature in APDU chunks. (3) Bind: the attestation message includes the FSBL-forwarded secure digest (BOOT-03 handoff), so the proof says 'this die, these SEs, this measured image'.
rationale: Trezor (ML-DSA-44 MCU cert + OPTIGA + TROPIC01), Ledger (SE genuine check) and BitBox (device attestation) all ship post-sale genuineness checks; pq1 has none, so a swapped SE or cloned unit is invisible once the SWD window has passed. Donjon showed attestation keyed from an MCU-held secret only proves possession — hence binding to the measurement and to DHUK (per-die, RDP-2-only final) rather than a flash secret.

risks: Variant constraint: only SE050 C/E/F carry factory attestation certs (the pq1 bench board is an E2 — confirm the production part). A C10 attestation is 4008 B + cert ≈ 5 KB per proof over 64-B HID (Trezor hit the same with ML-DSA and chunked, PR #6893). The per-use C10 keygen costs <1 s. Does not see a board-level implant on the display SPI (out of scope here). Factory HSM compromise still yields valid units until the transparency log exists (#68).
